paper_title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neur
core_problem: Integrating Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANNs) with the Theory of Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) for data-driven modeling.
methodology_summary: Employing a purely data-driven generalization of PCE (introduced in 2012 by Oladyshkin and Nowak) to construct a multi-variate orthonormal polynomial basis (aPC representation) based only on 2d raw stochastic moments evaluated from limited data.
datasets_eval: Available data set of limited size (used for moment evaluation).
empirical_results: The resulting polynomials are real if and only if the Hankel matrix of moments is positive definite. Numerical solutions for the linear system can be obtained via lower-order moments, recursive relations, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, or Stieltjes procedure.
explicit_limitations: For a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains undetermined/unspecified in the provided context.
